title: 176th Engineers assist with wildfires
description: Members of the Washington National Guard's 176th Engineer Company assist Washington State Department of Natural Resources with mop-up procedures on the Jolly Mountain Fire burning north of Cle Elum, Washington, September 9, 2017. Mop-up procedures include extinguishing smoldering materials and clearing debris that may be able to catch fire after a wildfire has moved through the area. (U.S. Army National Guard video by SPC Bradey Pettit)

transcript.text: I had a chance two years back to volunteer during the fires, but they already had enough volunteers.
This year though, they were pretty good about informing me of them wanting to get people in on this.
So this is my first year volunteering for fires.
So far on the ground we've been doing what is called mop-up.
So we're basically in a line going through and searching for fire for spot fires or routes that are on fire.
Essentially we're trying to make sure that the fires do not restart again.
And yeah, we're basically going around the trees, stumps, or if we see smoke coming up, we go there, we take a look.
And then we use the tools that we were given to put them out.
And we use the help of the other firefighting teams. We get some water hoses and just put them out making sure that they won't start up again.
And we do that from sun up to sundown essentially.
And what so far? Well, I do love nature. I like going on frecks and walks.
